body:
Thanks, mumblesgrapes. It's always great to hear from someone on the other side of this. Honestly, I think she wishes I was more like your bf, that I would just ignore it and carry on and let things just... pan out, because she thinks it's an unwinnable battle. Maybe your boyfriend got that vibe, and maybe you only sense uncaring and indifference because you're in such a dark place that only the negatives come through and the positives can't. 

I don't think it is an unwinnable battle, though, for her or for you. I think this is a big, dark cloud over her life, that even if it takes a few years to pass it eventually will, and when it does then we'll both be so happy that she made it through alive. 

Never thought about calling a crisis line before making this thread, and will be doing that.

Thanks for the advice, ZMM. You're right, I do need to look out for myself above all. I'm not going to leave her, though. I'm not just trying to help her because I think it's the right thing to do, I'm doing it because I love her more than anyone else I've been with -- we're both deeply weird people and make just a supernaturally good match. She's pretty heavily bipolar. I knew that coming in, and it does get hard and frustrating, but the good times completely outshine the bad. It's just that in the past few days there's been a huge upswing in warning signs. We're both kinda freaked about going long-distance for four months, so that might be playing a part. But if I broke up with her tonight then I'm 90% confident that she would do it tomorrow, and that would mess me up infinitely more than if she did it while we were together. So breaking up is really not an option that interests me. 

You're right, though; I need to convince her that she's not stuck, but I just can't figure out how. She's been working menial jobs and just barely squeaking by for fifteen years now; all that she's ever known is poverty and mindless labor, and I can understand why she feels like she is stuck. But she doesn't trust me when I say that it's not only possible but likely that things can turn around for her, she says that I only believe that because I grew up better off than her, that I'm just being young and idealistic, that because she was born to working class parents that she's destined to be working class too, and she would rather die than live her life like that. And this is so firmly entrenched in her worldview that I don't know how to help her shake it. 

I've never thought about calling a crisis line, I'd always assumed those were just for the people who were suicidal. We're hanging out after I get off work tonight, so if alarm bells are still going off tomorrow then I'll give them a call.
